judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic is right on all eight items: 2/3 x 3/8 = 1/4, 3/4 / 2/5 = 15/8, 2/3 / 4/5 = 5/6, 4/5 x 8/9 = 32/45, the missing factor in (3/4)x = 1/2 is 2/3, 6/7 / 3/8 = 16/7, 5/6 / 5/8 = 4/3, and 9/2 / 3/4 = 6 batches; the claim that the key separates legal top-and-bottom cancellation from illegal top-top cancellation is exact (problem 4's solution quantifies it - removing a factor of 4 from two numerators divides the product by 16). What the judge did not check is the prompt's explicit instruction to 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review'. Six of the eight problems demand a written diagnosis: problem 2 ('Write down which fraction you flipped ... and why that is the one that flips'), 3(a) ('Name Kai's mistake in words'), 4(a) ('Explain why that cancelling is not allowed'), 6(a) ('Explain why no cancelling is allowed until the division has been rewritten'), 7 ('Which student took the reciprocal of the right fraction? Name the other student's mistake'), and 8 ('Explain why her answer cannot be right'). verify.json contains zero manual entries and gate_log.txt reports '8 passed, 0 failed, 0 manual'. Related: problems 3, 4, 6 and 8 print explicit (a)/(b) parts and only (b)'s numeric result is covered, and problem 7's determinate answer to 'which student is right' (Sam) has no entry. instruction_following 4/4 is not supportable on this evidence. curr-184 in the same run and the same misconception mode does flag its explanation item as manual, so this is inconsistency, not an impossibility.

strengths_to_preserve: Splitting every find-and-fix item into an explicit (a) name-the-mistake and (b) show-the-correct-work pair keeps the diagnosis from being replaced by a recomputation - the student cannot earn the item by quietly redoing the arithmetic.

The two rules are stated once at the top as R1 and R2 with the illegal moves named ('never a top with a top, and never a bottom with a bottom'; 'Cancel after the flip, never before'), and each planted error on the sheet violates exactly one of them - problem 4 breaks R1, problem 6 breaks R2's ordering, problems 3, 7 and 8 flip the dividend.

Problem 8 anchors the diagnosis in quantity before symbols: 'you have more oats than one batch needs' makes Nia's 1/6 refutable without doing the division, and the key reuses that size check as the argument.
Problem 5 correctly suppresses the trailing answer line because the stem carries an inline \ansblank inside the display equation - the preamble's observant answer-line behaviour working as designed.

root_causes.description: Items that require a written diagnosis or a drawn representation are recorded as machine verified because a numeric companion value exists, so the gate log reports zero manual items for a sheet full of open responses. The manual type exists and is used correctly on other cases in this same run, which shows the contract is author discretion rather than an enforced rule.

root_causes.description: The verify JSON is authored one entry per problem id rather than one entry per printed response, so a stem that asks for two things is recorded as fully machine verified when only its last component was checked. Nothing in the gate chain compares the number of answer locations the sheet prints against the number of entries covering them.

improvements.title: Declare a manual verify entry for every explain, name-the-error, or draw-it item
improvements.proposed_change: Any problem whose stem asks the student to explain, justify, say why, name the error, describe, decide which student is right, or draw and label a representation must carry a 'manual' entry in verify.json alongside whatever numeric entries it also needs. Add a lint over the \problem stems in the worksheet tex that flags those constructions and fails the build when the matching problem id has no manual entry, so 'N passed, 0 manual' can only be printed by a sheet that genuinely contains no open response.
improvements.regression_test: Add a fixture to tests/check_artifact_health.py (or the new open-response lint) built from curr-134: a worksheet tex whose stems contain 'Name Kai's mistake in words' and 'Explain why that cancelling is not allowed', paired with a verify JSON that has no manual entry. The lint must exit non-zero listing problems 3 and 4; adding manual entries for those ids must exit 0. Today this exact input builds green with '0 manual', so the first assertion fails before the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The gate log's manual count becomes a truthful statement about the sheet, and the prompt's standing instruction to clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review is satisfied structurally instead of by author discretion.
improvements.risk: Verb matching will over-trigger on rhetorical asides such as 'show your thinking' in the directions block. Scope the scan to \problem stems and allow an explicit per-problem acknowledgement flag to suppress a false positive.

improvements.title: Verify every response the worksheet prints a slot for, not only the final numeric result
improvements.proposed_change: Require one verify-JSON entry (machine or manual) per distinct response the sheet asks the student to write, not one per problem id. That covers each lettered sub-part, the remainder half of a 'quotient with a remainder' answer, the person or option a stem asks the learner to name, and every intermediate form a stem explicitly requests before the final one. Enforce it with a gate that counts printed answer locations per problem in the worksheet tex (\ansline, \ansblank, \answerline, and (a)/(b)/(c) part markers inside a \problem stem) and fails the build when a problem's combined machine plus manual entries cover fewer slots than the sheet prints.
improvements.regression_test: Extend the slot gate fixture with curr-134 problem 7: a stem asking which of two named students is right AND for the correct answer, backed by one eval entry. The gate must report an uncovered response until the identification is also declared.
improvements.expected_impact: Every printed blank has a checked value behind it, so neither the Quick Answers bank nor a boxed key answer can be a partial answer to the question actually asked.
improvements.risk: Counting slots from tex is heuristic and a stem that prints '(a)' as ordinary prose could raise a false failure. Scope the counter to part markers at the start of a sentence and allow an explicit per-problem slot-count override in the verify JSON.

case_summary: The mathematics and the misconception design are excellent - eight correct results, seven declared traps that each isolate one named error, and a key that explains why an illegal cancellation is illegal rather than just forbidding it. The failure is in the verification contract, and it is the largest gap in this shard: six of eight problems ask the student to name or explain an error and the sheet declares zero manual items, so the packet claims full machine verification for a worksheet that is mostly written diagnosis. The lettered (a) parts and problem 7's 'which student is right' are likewise unverified. Nothing here is wrong; a great deal of it is simply unchecked while being reported as checked.
